title: The Personal Archive as Succession Infrastructure
author: RN Collins
principle: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

narrativeSequence.caption: A personal archive becomes succession infrastructure when it preserves not only the work, but the founder’s decision logic, rights evidence, relationships, access pathways, and instructions for future interpretation.
An accession-quality record preserves a house object beyond the founder’s lifetime while keeping the object, maker attribution, and museum stewardship distinct.

01 · CAPTURE — What cannot be reconstructed later?. Record why a choice was made, who contributed, what failed, what remains sensitive, and which relationship holds tacit knowledge. Use audio when voice carries nuance the file cannot.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 02 · PAIR — Can the physical and digital records find one another?. Pair garments, samples, notebooks, photographs, contracts, communications, and born-digital files through stable identifiers and relationship fields.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 03 · PRESERVE — Will the record open and remain trustworthy?. Maintain master and backup copies, record checksums and formats, document transformations, migrate deliberately, and keep known gaps visible.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 04 · AUTHORIZE — Who may act after absence?. Name stewards, alternates, access rules, privacy limits, conservation referrals, legal instruments, and a review process for loans, publication, licensing, interpretation, and disposal.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

mapping.prompt: Complete a seven-day sample across work, communications, rights, relationships, credentials, objects, and oral history.
Pair each physical object to its digital and documentary relatives.
Create two verified copies and record format, checksum, location, and migration need.
Take the authority map—not merely the boxes—to archivist, conservator, counsel, tax adviser, and successor as appropriate.
